subtitles.text: Looking into the distance, humans encountered something that resembled what was most intimate within themselves.
Researchers analyzing minute refractions of light from galaxies discovered an unexplained signal.
Similar signals were also detected by instruments on Earth and showed a correlation with changes in human emotion.
The signals remained detectable even after the person who had felt those emotions had left.
Following this discovery, emotion began to be understood as a phenomenon that left traces in the space beyond the body, rather than being confined to an individual’s inner life.
Emotional traces lingered in the same place, overlapping with those of other emotions.
Researchers called the fields formed by the accumulation and overlap of emotions in space “resonant fields.”
Yet it remained unclear whether these fields were formed solely by human emotions, whether other beings also influenced them, and how they were related to the patterns discovered in space.
Researchers observing resonant fields discovered living beings within them.
These unknown beings could not be classified as belonging to any known species and were thought to have existed for a long time.
Before their nature was fully understood, personal detectors and service apps became widely available, and people began observing these unknown beings through detectors.
People found them in their homes and in places they frequented, gave them names, and registered them in apps.
These emergent entities, which people observed and formed relationships with in everyday life, came to be called companion entities.
The apps translated signal strength and duration, distribution and recurrence into the language of personality, mood, intimacy, and attachment.
The unknown companion entities became characters that could be found and cared for on a screen.
On the day you arrived here, there was a dog stretched out where you took shelter from the pouring rain.
Under the narrow eaves, the dog opened its eyes but did not move aside.
In an unfamiliar city, the face of the dog you encountered each day became familiar.
Some days, the wag of its tail as it lay there kept you from simply walking past.
Among the many names people used for the same dog was the name you had given it.
You set down the food you had brought beside a water bowl someone had left.
In the spot where the dog always rested, you discovered a companion entity.
It was a fixed-type companion entity.
Fixed-type companion entities are known to live around feelings of attachment, trust, and long-standing loss.
You could not tell whether it had arisen from the dog or from your own feelings as you watched it.
On days when you did not encounter the dog, you examined the companion entity that remained there and tried to imagine how the dog had been.
With repeated observation, the entity’s signal grew steadier, and the app’s intimacy score rose.
To keep observing the companion entity was also to hold it in a recognizable form.
One day, the dog stopped appearing.
No one knew where it had gone.
Even as the dog remained absent, the companion entity remained in the same spot.
You knew that the entity was not the dog, yet it felt as though something had not quite left.
The companion entity there was always composed, peaceful, and gentle.
You began to worry that it, too, might disappear.
Not wanting to introduce other influences into the resonant field, you tried to remain as calm as possible while you were there.
On days when you were angry or very sad, you practiced leaving those feelings elsewhere before approaching the spot.
Because it seemed that if your feelings mingled with what was there, the companion entity that remained might change.
On the day you were told you had to leave this city, you were walking home alone when you saw a mass of jellyfish that had drifted into the harbor.
Contracting and expanding their bodies, the jellyfish kept drifting in on the same waves, without end.
Where they gathered, a signal similar to the one at the dog’s resting place was detected.
The companion entity among the jellyfish was also a fixed type, closely resembling the one at the dog’s spot.
Beside the jellyfish carried in by the currents, what had accumulated and overlapped to become a companion entity that stayed in one place for so long?
People called the influx of jellyfish into the harbor an invasion, but waves have no borders.
Having a home here did not give you the right to stay.
Even after your departure date was set, you walked your usual routes and stopped at familiar spots.
After the jellyfish were gone, the companion entity by the water remained in the same place.
You continued to observe the companion entities where the dog and the jellyfish had been.
Even though you had given them names, companion entities bound to the fabric of a place cannot go elsewhere.
The companion entities remained there, but you were denied a place to stay.
Even after you leave, your feelings will remain here, lingering in someone else’s scene.
People realized that no space was ever entirely empty.
Recognizing one another changed the conditions of existence.
No one could place themselves outside the world.
People called this era the end of solitude.
